facts: June 1961 Kennedy met Khrushchev in Vienna. 14 October 1962 a U-2 photographed Soviet missile sites in Cuba. 22 October Kennedy told the nation; 23 October he signed a naval quarantine of Cuba. 25 October Adlai Stevenson showed the photos at the UN. 28 October Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles; America secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey. The missiles were dismantled in November.

lines.say: In June 1961, a young President Kennedy met the Soviet leader, Nikita Khrushchev, in Vienna. It went badly.
On October 14th, 1962, an American spy plane photographed Soviet missile sites being built in Cuba, ninety miles from Florida.
Kennedy told the nation the missiles were there, and signed a naval quarantine of Cuba.
American warships moved in, and Soviet ships were still sailing towards the line.
At the United Nations, Adlai Stevenson showed the world the photographs.
After thirteen days, Khrushchev agreed to take the missiles out. In secret, America agreed to remove its own from Turkey.
By November, the missile sites were being taken apart.
